one_liner: Qt-based C++20 ORM whose own MySQL driver layer replaces QtSql/QMYSQL; measured gain is marginal (~40 ms per 620 queries).
what_it_does: TinyORM is a Laravel-Eloquent-style ORM and query builder for Qt 6 applications (MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQLite). TinyDrivers is its optional SQL layer, with TinyMySql as the only finished driver: it mirrors the QtSql API 1:1 (SqlDatabase, SqlQuery, Orm::Drivers namespace) and is swapped for QtSql at build time via the CMake BUILD_DRIVERS / BUILD_MYSQL_DRIVER / DRIVERS_TYPE options or the qmake build_*_drivers options, so TinyORM code needs no changes. It links directly against the MySQL C connector (libmysql/mysqlclient) or MariaDB Connector/C and drops the QtSql dependency, but still needs QtCore.
how_it_is_fast: There is no new algorithm: TinyMySql is a thin, KCacheGrind-tuned wrapper over the MySQL C API (mysql_real_query plus mysql_store_result for normal queries, mysql_stmt_* with bound buffers for prepared ones). Its small savings come from avoiding some per-value conversions, e.g. integer columns from prepared statements are built straight into a QVariant from the bound buffer without a QString::fromUtf8 round trip, and binding buffers are pre-reserved. The author states that about 90% of the time is spent inside the MySQL C API waiting on the server, so the driver layer has little left to speed up.
when_to_use: You already use TinyORM with MySQL or MariaDB and want to drop the QtSql module (smaller Qt footprint, fewer Qt plugins to deploy).
You want MySQL connection options QMYSQL handles awkwardly, such as valueless non-flag options or MYSQL_OPT_SSL_MODE verify_ca / verify_identity.
You prefer exceptions over QtSql's bool-plus-lastError() error reporting in a Qt 6, C++20 code base built on MSVC, GCC 11.2-14.2 or Clang 15+ (libstdc++).
You need a static, shared or runtime-loadable (dlopen / LoadLibrary) driver build that you control instead of Qt's plugin loader.
when_not_to_use: You want measurable query-latency gains: the author's own conclusion is that performance is 'very similar to QtSql'; database round trips dominate.
You use PostgreSQL or SQLite through TinyORM: TinyDrivers implements MySQL only, so those databases still need QtSql.
You need multiple result sets: SqlQuery::nextResult() is not implemented (only the first result set of a multi-statement query can be fetched).
You target macOS or Clang with libc++: unsupported per the supported-compilers page; Qt 5 support was dropped in v0.38.0.
You need an actively developed driver: the last commit is 2024-08-26 and TinyDrivers is v0.2.0; the official vcpkg port does not include it.

integration.form: static lib | shared lib (also a runtime-loadable TinyMySql module), built with CMake >=3.22 or qmake
integration.dependencies: QtCore (Qt >=6.2), range-v3 >=0.11.0, tabulate, MySQL Connector/C (libmysql/mysqlclient) or MariaDB Connector/C; QtSql is not needed when TinyDrivers is enabled
integration.min_toolchain: C++20; MSVC 2019 16.9+ / 2022, GCC 11.2-14.2, Clang 15+ with libstdc++, clang-cl 15+
integration.platforms: Windows 10+ and Linux; macOS and libc++ not supported
integration.thread_safety: A connection may be used only from the thread that created it; multi-threading is disabled on Clang <14.0.3 (MSYS2), Clang <14.0.4 (Linux) and GCC on MSYS2 because of thread_local TLS-wrapper bugs; the schema builder and migrations are not thread-safe. TinyMySql calls mysql_thread_end() when a thread's connection is torn down.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: 1:1 QtSql API swapped at compile time for TinyORM users, but MySQL only, errors are thrown as exceptions (bool-returning methods always return true), exec(QString) no longer simulates prepared statements, and nextResult() is missing

gotchas: Error semantics differ from QtSql: code that checks a false return and then lastError() will never see the error, because TinyDrivers throws instead.
Normal and prepared queries always buffer the whole result set on the client (mysql_store_result / mysql_stmt_store_result); there is no streaming mode, so very large SELECTs cost client memory.

Harness flaw behind the 40 ms figure: TinyOrmPlayground's only timer (QElapsedTimer in src/main.cpp) wraps the whole run, including connectToDatabase(), connection creation and per-query console logging with title headers, against a live MySQL server, in a Debug build, one run; the total time is never published, so the gap cannot be separated from server and logging noise.
The playground has since grown to ~1600 queries (TinyORM README), so the 620-query configuration behind the claim is no longer the default and cannot be re-run from published material.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No siblings catalogued yet in database-client-drivers; within the catalogue the closest neighbour is ODB (a compiled C++ ORM), and TinyDrivers is only worth picking if you are already on TinyORM and Qt and want to shed QtSql, not for speed.
verified_claims_summary: The author reports that TinyOrmPlayground (620 MySQL queries) finished about 40 ms sooner with TinyDrivers/TinyMySql than with QtSql/QMYSQL, built with GCC 13.2.1 in Debug mode on Linux, one run, no CPU model, no total runtime and no variance; the same page calls the two 'very similar' because 90% of the time is spent in the MySQL C API. Roughly 65 microseconds per query of driver overhead at most, with the timer also covering connection setup and console logging.
status_note: Stale: no commits since 2024-08-26 (5,739 commits; maintainer still closing issues in 2025, e.g. #69 in Sep 2025), MIT-licensed and copyable, but tied to Qt 6 and TinyORM's own build system, with open Windows build/dllexport issues (#55, #61, #63, #65).
